text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: CRITICAL - kubelet NotReady on host `gpu-rt-7-21` (pd_incident/INC-4221) -- triggered by node healthcheck. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-4221

oncall_aly: acked. I'm on it. Pulling node state now.

oncall_aly: `kubectl get nodes gpu-rt-7-21 -o wide` shows `NotReady` + LastSeen: 00:01:02. Scheduling pods evicted?

eng_jamie: seeing increased 5xx from rack-7 inference pool in dashboards (latency normal but 503 spikes). tagging product: @cs_lia

oncall_aly: running `kubectl describe node gpu-rt-7-21` -> Kubelet reports: "node not ready: kubelet is not responding". Trying `ssh gpu-rt-7-21`... ssh times out.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: GPU node unresponsive -> https://wiki.redwood/ops/runbooks/gpu-node-unresponsive

oncall_aly: trying `mtr` to host IP, nothing. ping drops. Looks like host-level network or kernel.hang. Initiating cordon to stop scheduling new pods: `kubectl cordon gpu-rt-7-21`

oncall_aly: cordon ok. Next: drain safe? we should force-delete pods if kubelet not responding. Putting quick note: this may evict live inference connections, but cluster autoscaler has headroom in other racks.

sre_mike: I'm waking up, on my way. If ssh dead, we should mark host for maintenance and failover. I'll take hardware fallback/host reprovision after handoff.

oncall_aly: running graceful drain (30s timeout) -> most pods stuck terminating because kubelet not responding. Using force drain: `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0 -l node=gpu-rt-7-21`

eng_jamie: confirmed traffic routed off the node; error rate for model-serving group decreased a bit but still ~1.8% over baseline. Looks like some clients retried; CS notified.

cs_lia: preparing customer advisory for impacted customers (inference-rack-7): will send initial note (no PII) that we're mitigating node outage, ETA unknown.

oncall_aly: checked metrics: NVML cgroup shows GPU unreachable errors in last 2m, `dmesg` would help but host is unreachable. Kernel oops suspected.

ops-runbook-bot: Suggested next steps: mark host for reprovision -> `kubectl label node gpu-rt-7-21 maintenance=true` and open ticket to infra-hardware.

oncall_aly: added maintenance label. Opening infra ticket now: TICKET-8891 created to request rack tech to power-cycle host and run diagnostics. Link: https://tickets.internal/TICKET-8891

sre_mike: taking over primary oncall. I'll escalate to hardware & infra. @oncall_aly you're free to hand off. Mike -> I'm going to attempt out-of-band management (IPMI) and run `journalctl -k -b -1` if I get console.

oncall_aly: handoff to @sre_mike : handing off context + timeline. All cordon/drain actions done. PD incident updated and ack moved to Mike. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: PagerDuty: ACK by sre_mike (escalation policy: hw-team).

sre_mike: pinging hw-team, requesting immediate rack visit. Attempting IPMI console now. If console shows kernel panic, we'll collect `vmcore` and NVMe SMART info. Standby. :eyes:

sre_mike: IPMI login success, serial shows repeated oops: "kernel panic - not syncing: upstream bug" + trace referencing `nvidia_uvm`. Copying snippet:```
[   42.128947] NVRM: GPU at 0000:5e:00.0: GPU fault detected: Xid 79
[   42.128951] kernel: Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
```

sre_mike: that's a kernel/GPU driver crash. I'll mark host as decommission for now and reprovision replacement. Starting automated reprovision job: `infra-provision --replace gpu-rt-7-21 --reason kernel-panic`

eng_jamie: can we confirm failover completed for long-running customer jobs? We have a small queue that might have lost in-flight requests. Monitoring ingestion logs.

cs_lia: drafting to customers: short note saying some in-flight inference requests may have failed; we routed work to healthy capacity and retries succeeded for most customers. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary.

sre_mike: infra-provision job queued, ETA for replacement VM GPU host ~ 18 mins (auto image + kube join). I'll keep updates here.

incident-bot: Created incident document: https://incidents.internal/INC-4221 (status: investigating).

sre_mike: taking ownership of incident on-call. Live runbook steps executed: cordon, force-evict, label maintenance, open ticket, reprovision started. Notified CS.

oncall_aly: thanks, handing off fully. Leaving notes in ticket about observed Xid 79/NVRM.

sre_mike: quick postmortem notes to capture: suspected culprit: NVIDIA kernel driver + kernel mismatch after recent host kernel update; action items: 1) block that kernel image on rack-7 images 2) add kernel/driver compatibility check before host rollouts 3) add automated early-warning for Xid 79 in metrics. Assigning to eng_jamie and infra-team.

eng_jamie: ack, will own compatibility check. I'll create a short eval to run GPU stress + driver check in pre-deploy.

sre_mike: update 18m: replacement host joined cluster, pods scheduled, no new 503 spikes observed. Marking incident as mitigated, but leaving incident open until postmortem.

cs_lia: sent initial customer advisory to affected accounts. Will follow up with postmortem.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: RESOLVED by sre_mike.

sre_mike: closing notes: mitigation complete, root cause likely driver/kernel regression on gpu-rt-7-21 causing kernel panic (Xid 79). Postmortem ticket created: PM-5643.

cs_lia: thanks team. I'll schedule external digest after postmortem. :memo:

oncall_aly: good job everyone.

sre_mike: leaving for 1st-line follow-up. If anyone sees recurring Xid 79 in rack-7, please page. :hammer_and_wrench:

(reacted :thumbsup: by eng_jamie)
